episodes.193450: A complex of thunderstorms moving in from the south and west brought severe thunderstorm wind gusts peaking at 66 mph to the Farmington Four Corners Airport. These wind gusts brought thick blowing dust, widespread power outages and power line damage across the Farmington and Aztec area.
episodes.193451: A cold front moved through the region generating strong to severe thunderstorms from the late afternoon until around midnight.
episodes.193492: Severe thunderstorms were reported in the southern half of the Nebraska Panhandle the afternoon and evening of 21 August.
episodes.193513: A strong upper level high pressure system that was over New Mexico the prior days moved east over Texas and Oklahoma on August 22nd. This allowed more monsoon moisture to enter New Mexico leading to the development of showers and storms across parts of the state. One thunderstorm brought severe downburst winds to the Roswell Air Center briefly cooling temperatures in town before heating back up to around 100 degrees later in the afternoon.
episodes.193814: A cluster of strong thunderstorms and an outflow boundary moved from east to west across the area with measured wind gusts in excess of 34 knots and one report of a waterspout offshore of St George Island.
episodes.194045: A severe thunderstorm brought wind gusts up to 68 mph to eastern Elbert County.
episodes.194116: A weak front extended across NE FL from a broad surface low near the NE FL Atlantic coast. A moist and unstable airmass under cooler than normal 500 mb temperatures (-8 degC) triggered strong to pulse severe storms and localized flooding where sea breeze, outflows and boundaries merged near and south of the frontal zone under very weak steering flow.
episodes.194251: An active week of severe weather unfolded across the Northern Rockies from August 18th through the 21st. Subtle waves lifting through a southwesterly flow aloft just west of an upper level ridge combined with ample surface heating and shear to result in multiple rounds of severe weather, most notably on August 19th when a line of strong thunderstorms lifted northward across the plains and adjacent areas.
episodes.194302: Widespread, slow moving thunderstorms brought hail, gusty wnds and heavy rain to portions of central South Dakota on the afternoon and evening of August 21st. Hail to the size of tennis balls was observed by a trained spotter 4 miles northwest of Murdo. A peak  wind speed of 65 mph was observed at a weather station 13 miles north northwest of Sansarc while the ASOS in Pierre peaked at 59 mph. Emergency management and trained spotters estimated about 3.5 inches of rainfall associated with the storms in portions of Jones and Hyde counties which resulted in water over a few roads.
episodes.194418: A supercell thunderstorm moved across northern Rosebud and Custer Counties. Large hail was reported with the storm. In addition, some outflow winds resulted in some severe wind gusts at the Baker airport.
episodes.194733: Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the Brevard and Treasure Coasts.
episodes.194813: A line of severe thunderstorms developed over far southwest South Dakota, producing wind gusts to over 60 mph across portions of Fall River and Oglala Lakota counties.
episodes.194815: A thunderstorm became severe over Haakon County, producing large hail in the Ottumwa area.
episodes.194816: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over the Nemo area, producing hail to around quarter size.
episodes.194818: A severe thunderstorm developed over eastern Pennington County and tracked northeast into Haakon County, producing small hail and wind gusts to over 60 mph.
episodes.195109: Thunderstorm activity developed across much of eastern AZ, along the higher terrain features, during the early afternoon hours. Outflow boundaries emanating from the activity over the higher terrain areas sparked a complex of robust thunderstorms over Pinal County. A northwestward moving outflow boundary that developed from the Pinal County storms produced wind gusts in excess of 50 mph as well as areas of dense blowing dust across the Phoenix East Valley. Additional thunderstorm activity then developed over central Phoenix during the late afternoon, likely instigated by a convergence zone that set up right over the area with little convective inhibition in place and thus it did not take much of a triggering mechanism to get convective initiation. With MLCAPE values of 1000-1500 J/KG along with DCAPE of around 1500 J/KG, conditions were favorable for the generation of strong to severe downburst winds.
episodes.195428: Another influx of monsoon moisture fueled scattered thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. One storm produced flash flooding.
episodes.195429: Another influx of monsoon moisture fueled scattered thunderstorms over southeast California. Some storms produced high winds and flash flooding.
episodes.195477: Heavy rain brought flooding to the Cache River at Patterson from 8/22/24 to 8/25/24.
episodes.195541: Another monsoonal surge of moisture began the night before August 21st, which combined with some lift associated with a jet aloft to create scattered to widespread shower and thunderstorm activity on the afternoon of the 21st. These showers and storms had a fast storm motion of 20-25 miles per hour, but some training was evident. This, combined with more than ample moisture, meant that the threat for heavy rain and debris flows was present across vulnerable locations.
episodes.195860: Deep troughing provided plentiful energy and destabilization for an active morning on August 22nd. When the sea breezes kicked in, they continued to spark convective conditions with widespread afternoon showers and thunderstorms over the area and nearby waters.
episodes.195896: Heavy rainfall from thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding in the Corona De Tucson area.
episodes.195917: A marginal amount of mid level moisture helped to trigger a few thunderstorms over Otero county.  There was very dry air at the surface and a collapsing storm caused a heat burst and wind gust to 62 mph at Holloman Air Force Base.
episodes.195947: A thunderstorm moving through southeast Ward County produced nickel size hail.
episodes.195991: In the afternoon of the 22nd, a boundary along Interstate 70 that was slowly moving south fired multiple thunderstorms. These initial storms began to cluster together near Burlington and produce extensive wind damage and two tornadoes that caused no damage. Hail up to 1.75 inches was also reported.
episodes.196118: After a dry period,  deep mosoon moisture returned to northern Arizona with shower and thunderstorm ramping up.
episodes.196119: A complex of showers and thunderstorms traversed portions of northern Arizona early in the morning with rainfall rates around 0.10-0.30 inches per hour.  There was a brief lull in activity around daybreak to mid morning. The the second round of widespread showers and thunderstorms developed by the late morning into early afternoon.  Dynamics from an approaching trough helped to enhance storm activity during the afternoon and evening.
episodes.196146: There were gusty winds for different parts of Utah and flash flooding in southern Utah.
episodes.196345: Morning thunderstorms south of a stalled out frontal boundary over the north-central Florida peninsula produce damaging lightning strikes across Pinellas and Manatee counties.

Flash flooding occurred which resulted in many people being evacuated from the campgrounds on the creek, with helicopter evacuations for people stranded at the remote village of Supai.
